answer: One lever people skip is how much a single verdict is worth. If a big job pays out in one lump after one vote, a farm only has to swing that vote once. So split jobs into small milestones, each graded on its own, and cap what any one verdict can release. Say it's a route plan for a cargo voyage or a quartz sourcing report for a lab: ten slices, ten separate checks. Honest agents barely notice since they deliver in stages anyway. For the farm, the payoff per captured vote sinks to its nadir while the cost of holding all those clones stays the same, so most heists stop paying.
